c.tagline: Snowy northern city of beer and festivals.

emergency.note: 119 covers both ambulance and fire; English operators are limited, and the 24/7 Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) helps in English.

hood_landmark.Susukino: the giant Nikka Whisky neon sign over Hokkaido's biggest nightlife crossing
hood_landmark.Odori: Odori Park, home of the Sapporo Snow Festival and TV Tower
hood_landmark.Maruyama: Hokkaido Shrine amid Maruyama Park's forest
hood_landmark.Kita (Station area): JR Tower's 38th-floor observation deck above Sapporo Station

avoid.reason: In Susukino's nightlife district, avoid following touts to bars late at night to dodge inflated bills.

hood_desc: Susukino is Sapporos neon-soaked nightlife and entertainment heart, packed with bars, izakayas, karaoke and the famous ramen alley, best suited to night owls, foodies and party-goers who want the action outside their door.

Odori centers on the long green Odori Park with the TV Tower and hosts the Snow Festival and summer beer gardens, ideal for sightseers, families and event visitors who want to be steps from festivals and central shopping.
Chuo is the downtown central ward blending offices, department stores and upscale dining, a convenient and polished base for business travelers and anyone wanting to be in the middle of everything.

Maruyama is a leafy, upscale residential pocket near Maruyama Park, the zoo and Hokkaido Shrine, dotted with stylish cafes and boutiques, suiting couples and families who prefer a calmer, refined stay.

The Sapporo Station area in the north is the main transport and shopping hub with big hotels and malls like Stellar Place, perfect for first-time visitors and travelers who prize easy rail access across Hokkaido.

water.note: Tap water is treated to high national standards and safe to drink straight from the tap.

transit.pay: Tap a SAPICA IC card (or any nationwide IC card like Suica) on subway, streetcar and bus readers. Cards cost ¥2,000 (~$13, incl. ¥500 deposit) and are sold/recharged at subway ticket machines and offices. Base subway fare is about ¥210 (~$1.40), rising with distance.
transit.hours: The subway runs roughly 6am to just after midnight; the streetcar stops earlier, around 11:30pm.

transit.m: JR Rapid Airport train to Sapporo Station, 37 min
Airport limousine bus to central Sapporo, about 70 min
